ios.desc:
UTM SE is a PC emulator that allows you to run classic software and old-school games.

* Supports both VGA mode for graphics and terminal mode for text-only operating systems
* Emulates x86, ARM, PPC, and RISC-V architectures
* Run pre-built machines or create your own configuration from scratch
* Built from QEMU, a powerful and widely used emulator

quotes.text: Apple somewhat lifted the emulator restrictions on the App Store which means you can install UTM from here: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/utm-se-retro-pc-emulator/id1564628856

quotes.text:
There‘s UTM SE on the App Store, which might be ok to use for very minimal distros (no JIT): https://apps.apple.com/at/app/utm-se-retro-pc-emulator/id1564628856?l=en-GB

If you had a second spare iPhone, you could run it semi tethered with JIT and just any ARM/x86 OS: https://docs.getutm.app/installation/ios/

Though a JB would be more convenient. And things start to get interesting with M1 and its virtualization support.

iOS virtualization is already a mature thing: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/utm-se-retro-pc-emulator/id1564628856

Dev site: https://getutm.app/
